items.title: Mississauga ringleader of major terror plot granted full parole in Canada
items.summary: ” Zakaria Amara, of Mississauga, who helped recruit members for a group that aimed to storm Parliament Hill and bomb several locations around Toronto, has been on day parole with multiple conditions for four years, and the board upgraded his release after reviewing his case last week. ” It says he was closely supervised while on day parole and his internet use, friendships and relationships were monitored, with no reported safety concerns or breaches. ” He is barred from communicating with anyone involved in criminal activity, including any of the others arrested in the June 2006 anti-terrorist raids, or come into contact with anyone with extremist ideologies, except in his work as a consultant with a specialized program. He must also continue to participate in counselling and be subject to financial monitoring as well as restrictions on his phone and internet use. The board’s decision comes two decades after the dismantling of the homegrown plot that shocked the country and shifted public discourse around terrorism.

items.title: Frost advisory issued for Mississauga, Brampton for Friday night, areas north of Highway 401 most likely to be impacted
items.summary: Environment Canada says freezing temperatures are expected the night of Friday, Oct. 16 into Saturday morning. Environment Canada has issued a frost advisory for Brampton and Mississauga. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued a frost advisory for Mississauga and Brampton Friday, Oct. 16. The national weather agency said freezing temperatures are expected at night and into Saturday morning. “Temperatures are expected to fall to near or slightly below the freezing mark overnight into Saturday morning, particularly for areas north of Highway 401,” the advisory said. Areas closer to Lake Ontario are expected to be a few degrees warmer. Environment Canada said damage to plants, trees, and crops is possible. People are advised to take preventive measures to protect cold-sensitive plants, trees, and crops.

items.title: A home in Mississauga or Brampton, at what cost? Housing market remains unattainable for most residents, while NIMBYism only makes it worse
items.summary: For most residents across Peel, the idea of defining themselves as property owners seems more like a mirage. The image appears tantalizingly before them, shimmering in their mind, but when they reach out for it…nothing is there. In Mississauga and Brampton, where the cost of buying a home ranks among the world’s top 15 least affordable places, even the mirage is growing more distant. Four years after being elected, Ontario Premier Doug Ford assigned ambitious new housing targets to 29 municipalities across the province: tasking Mississauga with onboarding 120,000 new homes by 2031, and Brampton with 113,000. What followed was a long, exhaustive list of sweeping legislative changes to accelerate development, many of which weakened environmental protections and eased restrictions on developers under the guise of making housing within reach for Ontarians. 5 million new homes by 2031. All three municipalities in the region of Peel are not on track to meet their housing goals set by the PC government. 3 percent of Peel’s population having “a household after-tax income of $150,000 or higher”, as per its latest census. The Region has reported that 80 percent of Peel’s residents cannot afford the cost of buying a home. 5 percent from the previous month. 5 percent or $31,090 from August 2026.

items.title: Mississauga Man Identified as Suspect in Yonge Street Attack on Pro-Palestinian Demonstrator
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a 20-year-old Mississauga man, Martin Salgatar, has been charged with aggravated assault after an alleged attack on a demonstrator during a pro-Palestinian rally in downtown Toronto. According to Toronto police, Salgatar surrendered to officers on Oct. 12, two days after the alleged assault near Yonge and Grosvenor streets on Saturday, Oct. 10. Investigators allege the victim was walking northbound on Yonge Street and talking with another demonstrator when the suspect approached from behind and punched the victim several times in the head without provocation. Police say the victim fell to the ground and sustained injuries to the face and leg. The outlet reports the Toronto Police Service's Hate Crime Unit is handling the investigation, which began with a public appeal for help identifying the suspect. Insauga.com says Salgatar was scheduled to appear at the Toronto Regional Bail Centre on Oct. 13.

items.title: House of the week: 3-storey semi-detached home with elevator in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: Three-storey semi-detached home with an elevator in Mississauga. Features: This semi-detached home offers over 4,400 square feet of living space with an elevator providing access to all floors. The main floor showcases tray ceilings, wide-plank light oak hardwood floors and expansive windows that fill the space with natural light. A marble fireplace anchors the living room. The kitchen features a large quartz island and high-end appliances. Glass doors lead to a landscaped backyard with a wood deck and a gas barbecue hookup. Upstairs, the primary bedroom has dual walk-in closets, an ensuite bathroom and a skylit hallway. Each additional bedroom includes walk-in closets and ensuite bathrooms. The third floor adds a flexible living space with two more bedrooms and a home office. The finished basement features a three-piece bathroom, a sauna and rough-ins for a second kitchen and laundry area. Additional highlights include a monitored smart home system, power blinds and an EV-ready epoxy garage. This home is steps away from Port Credit’s waterfront, boutique shopping, parks, dining, and it is also near GO Transit and the QEW.

items.title: Frost Advisory Issued for Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton as Temperatures Dip Toward Freezing Overnight
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Environment Canada has placed Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton under a yellow frost advisory as temperatures are expected to dip toward freezing overnight into Saturday morning. According to the forecaster, areas north of Highway 401 are expected to see temperatures fall to near or slightly below the freezing mark, while neighbourhoods closer to Lake Ontario will stay a few degrees warmer. Environment Canada says the frost could cause damage to plants, trees and crops. The outlet reports Toronto's overnight low is forecast at 0 C, or 3 C near the lake, with a 40 per cent chance of showers Friday evening. Insauga.com says northwest winds are expected to reach 40 km/h and gust to 60 km/h before easing to 20 km/h, gusting to 40 km/h, by morning.

items.title: Four Homes Razed as Edenshaw Breaks Ground on 30-Storey Port Credit Rental Tower
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Edenshaw Developments has broken ground on a 30-storey rental apartment building near the Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga, after demolishing four homes and a shed that previously occupied the site. According to the outlet, the project sits at 23 Elizabeth St. N. and 42-46 Park St., and a spokesperson for Edenshaw said demolition of the existing structures is nearly complete. The outlet reports the development has faced criticism before: a previous application for a 22-storey building on the same property was rejected by the Ontario Land Tribunal in 2023. Insauga.com says the height of the new 30-storey proposal remains a concern for some area residents. The outlet quotes a Facebook post from September in which a resident said surrounding buildings could be affected by privacy and overlook issues, shadow, wind, traffic, and construction dust and noise.

items.title: INSAUGA Poll Finds Mississauga Readers Skeptical a Subway Will Ever Reach the City
items.summary: Insauga.com reports a majority of respondents to its reader poll do not believe Mississauga will ever get a subway, despite billions of dollars being invested in rapid transit in the city. According to the outlet, the poll asked readers whether Mississauga will ever get a subway, and skeptics edged out those who think it will happen by a margin of 441 votes. The outlet notes Mississauga currently has no subway line and there are no announced plans to extend Toronto's subway system into the city. Insauga.com reports the city is nonetheless in the middle of one of the biggest transit transformations in its history. The outlet says the Hazel McCallion Line, formerly known as the Hurontario LRT, is under construction and will run about 18 kilometres between Port Credit GO Station in Mississauga and the Brampton Gateway Terminal at Steeles Avenue.

items.title: Advance Voting Turnout in Mississauga Jumps 57 Percent Ahead of Oct. 26 Election
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports a record surge in advance voting ahead of the city's Oct. 26 municipal election. According to data the city released Oct. 13, 44,049 residents cast ballots during advance polls held between Oct. 6 and 11, a 57 per cent increase from the 28,052 early voters recorded during the 2022 municipal election's advance polling window. The outlet reports the single busiest day was Oct. 11, when 12,335 ballots were cast. Mississauga.com says advance voting turnout has climbed steadily since 2018, when 19,188 residents voted early, rising to 24,731 during the June 2024 mayoral byelection. The outlet notes residents who missed the advance voting window can still cast a ballot on municipal election day, Oct. 26.
